title: New complementary python codes to locate Single Nucleotide Polymorphisms (SNPs) and Overlapping G-Quadruplex Sequences (G4s)
author: SAAD, Shebaby, et al.

steps.title: Install Python 3.9.7
steps.instruction: Download and install Python version 3.9.7 on the computer that will run the codes.

steps.title: Prepare SNP‑locator input files
steps.instruction: Create two text files: (1) a FASTA file containing the full genomic sequence of the target gene, and (2) a plain‑text file that records the genetic variant using the Human Genome Variation Society (HGVS) cDNA notation (e.g., c.506-1G>A).

substeps.instruction: Save the FASTA file with any name you choose (e.g., CYP2D6.fasta).
Write the variant exactly as defined by HGVS at the cDNA level.

steps.title: Run SNP‑locator code
steps.instruction: Execute the SNP‑locator Python script, supplying three mandatory arguments: the folder path containing the FASTA file, the FASTA file name, and the cDNA‑level mutation description. If the mutation lies in an intron, also provide two extra arguments indicating the intron direction (“+” for forward, “‑” for backward) and the intronic distance from the cDNA variant.

substeps.instruction: Open a command‑line window and navigate to the script directory.

steps.title: Save SNP‑locator results
steps.instruction: After the script finishes, copy the printed output (the SNP marked with quotation marks and the distance from the start codon) into a new text file as shown in the article’s Fig B.

steps.title: Generate G4 predictions with G4Hunter
steps.instruction: Submit the same genomic sequence to the G4Hunter web tool (http://bioinformatics.cruk.cam.ac.uk/G4Hunter/) and download the resulting G4‑sequence text file.

steps.title: Edit G4Hunter output file
steps.instruction: Open the G4Hunter result file and locate the line that begins with “seqnames”. For each gene, ensure the gene name appears alone on a line followed immediately by a “>” symbol (e.g., `CYP2D6>`). Adjust this formatting for every new gene before running the next script.

steps.title: Run G4‑overlap code
steps.instruction: Execute the G4‑overlap Python script, providing: (1) the folder path where both the SNP‑locator result file and the edited G4Hunter file reside, (2) the SNP‑locator result file name, and (3) the G4Hunter file name.

substeps.instruction: Open a command‑line window and navigate to the script directory.

steps.title: Interpret G4‑overlap results
steps.instruction: The script calculates: (a) the distance from each G4 start to the start codon, (b) the distance from the SNP to each of those values, stores all distances in a list, extracts the minimum distance, and repeats the process for every SNP variant. The final output lists, for each gene, the start position of the selected G4 sequence and its minimum distance to the SNP.
